# Schatunowsky — 30 is the largest number whose survivors are all prime

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean

Treat a number as a cycle; its survivors are the numbers below it sharing no factor with it. For 30 every survivor other than 1 is prime, and no larger number has this property (Schatunowsky, 1893). The ceiling forces the wheels; Bonse's inequality then caps the number.

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [Schatunowsky's Theorem (ProofWiki), after S. O. Shatunovsky (1893)](https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Schatunowsky's_Theorem) — the theorem this node proves; the classical proof uses the same ceiling argument
- [V. Pambuccian, Schatunowsky's theorem, Bonse's inequality, and Chebyshev's theorem in weak fragments of Peano arithmetic, Math. Log. Quart. 61 (2015)](https://doi.org/10.1002/malq.201400064) — shows Schatunowsky follows from Bonse's inequality, the route taken here
- [H. King and V. Pambuccian, Generalized Schatunowsky theorem in a weak arithmetic (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08256) — the generalization (Kaneko–Nakai) for survivors of the wheels above a fixed prime

## Claims

<a id="ceiling_forces_wheels"></a>
### `ceiling_forces_wheels`

If every survivor of a number is prime, every prime whose square lies below the number divides it.

```lean
/-- **The ceiling forces the wheels.** If every survivor of `N` is prime, then
every prime `p` whose square lies below `N` divides `N`. -/
def ceiling_forces_wheels : Prop :=
  ∀ N p : Nat, survivors_all_prime N → p.Prime → p * p < N → p ∣ N
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Schatunowsky.ceiling_forces_wheels_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Schatunowsky.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Schatunowsky.lean)

<a id="thirty_survivors_all_prime"></a>
### `thirty_survivors_all_prime`

Every survivor of 30 other than 1 is prime.

```lean
/-- **30 has the property**: every survivor of 30 other than 1 is prime. -/
def thirty_survivors_all_prime : Prop :=
  survivors_all_prime 30
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Schatunowsky.thirty_survivors_all_prime_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Schatunowsky.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Schatunowsky.lean)

<a id="schatunowsky_bound"></a>
### `schatunowsky_bound`

A number whose survivors are all prime is at most 30 (Schatunowsky's theorem).

```lean
/-- **Schatunowsky's theorem (1893).** A number whose survivors are all prime is
at most 30. -/
def schatunowsky_bound : Prop :=
  ∀ N : Nat, survivors_all_prime N → N ≤ 30
```

**Rests on:** [`BonseCeiling.ceiling_inside_cycle`](BonseCeiling.md#ceiling_inside_cycle)

**Proof:** `RNS.Schatunowsky.schatunowsky_bound_step` in [`RNSSolutions/Schatunowsky.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Schatunowsky.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)
